criteria.name: Quality of disagreement, trust and grounding

sub.example: T3 and T6 flag growth as conditional 'if'.

sub.name: Proportionate next steps
sub.example: T8 simulated commute for 14 days is cheap and concrete.
sub.limitation: Minor: section E 'inquire' step lacks specifics on what to ask.

sub.name: Accessible language
sub.example: Plain phrasing throughout; T8 instructions concrete.
sub.limitation: Minor: T2 'carriage of transit', T4 'marginal productivity' slightly opaque.

sub.name: Traceable arguments and references
sub.example: Each turn names whose point it answers, T2-T9.
sub.limitation: Material: T7 'as the Strategist suggests' maps to no clear turn.

sub.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
sub.example: Nine turns, each roughly 45 to 60 words.
sub.limitation: Minor: uniform turn rhythm, no short sharp exchanges.

sub.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
sub.example: Optimizer, Stoic, Strategist hold distinct positions.
sub.limitation: Material: all three use identical 'X claims... but' openers; voices sound alike.

sub.name: Economy and sustained attention
sub.example: T8 introduces fresh practical content late.
sub.limitation: Material: openers recap prior turns verbatim, e.g. T5, T6.

sub.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
sub.example: T5 frames commute as trading sovereignty for wage.
sub.limitation: Material: tension stays abstract; no concrete life cost named.

sub.name: Surprise and reversals
sub.example: T7 Optimizer abandons his T1 calculation.
sub.limitation: Material: T7 reversal has no traced cause from an earlier argument.

sub.name: Personality and expressive voice
sub.example: Stoic's T2 Seneca-flavoured line has some colour.
sub.limitation: Material: Optimizer and Strategist read as flat, templated voices.

sub.name: Memorable delivery
sub.example: T8: sit in a chair 90 minutes before and after work.
sub.limitation: Material: few analogies or sharp lines beyond T8.

sub.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
sub.example: T9 ends on a pointed question.
sub.limitation: Material: constant even intensity; no build or release across turns.

strengths: T8 simulated 14-day commute is a concrete, cheap test the user can run.
Section D frames sovereignty now versus leverage later, offering two motives as alternatives.
Three distinct positions (utility, finite life, optionality) each answer the prior speaker.
weaknesses: Personal relevance thin: no question on transit mode, current commute, remote days or family (all minds).
T7 Optimizer reversal lacks a traced cause and drops the useful hourly-wage calculation.
Templated 'X claims... but' openers flatten voices and recap prior turns, T2-T9.
editorNotes: Require at least two turns to pose questions on missing facts (transit mode, remote days, current commute) with what each answer implies.
Require any reversal to cite the specific earlier turn and argument that changed the speaker's mind.
Ban formulaic openers restating the prior speaker; require a mid-debate distinction that a later turn uses.
Ask for one countable threshold from the user's own numbers, e.g. effective hourly wage after commute.
